description: Casos clínicos de lectura de escáneres (Casos 8 al 15)
rules: Traducir SOLO los valores de texto al español, con un tono formal, médico, riguroso y pedagógico.
NO traducir identificadores, claves de objetos, ids de modalidad, nombres de archivo ni tags de código.
Conservar siglas técnicas e imagenológicas intactas (MRI, CT, PET, SPECT, fMRI, EEG, MEG, T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, ADC, BOLD, 3T, TR, TE, TI).
Conservar unidades de medida, cifras numéricas y marcadores de evidencia exactamente en su formato original.
El nombre de la marca 'Neuro Lightbox' no se traduce.
Devolver EXCLUSIVAMENTE el objeto JSON con las mismas claves y los valores traducidos al español.

glossary.SPECT: SPECT (Tomografía por emisión de fotón único)
glossary.BOLD: BOLD (dependiente del nivel de oxigenación sanguínea)

items.case_8.hx: 61-year-old smoker with weight loss and a lung mass. New unsteadiness and headache.
items.case_8.report: MRI with contrast: three small ring- and nodular-enhancing lesions at the grey–white junction, each with oedema out of proportion to its size.
case_8.teach: Metastases lodge at the grey–white junction, where vessels narrow.
Contrast MRI finds far more lesions than CT, which changes treatment.
Count them: a few lesions may be treated with radiosurgery.
items.case_9.hx: 27-year-old woman. Painful blurred vision in the right eye last year that recovered; now tingling in both legs.
items.case_9.report: MRI: multiple ovoid FLAIR-bright lesions around the lateral ventricles, oriented perpendicular to them, with juxtacortical lesions. One lesion enhances after gadolinium; the others do not.
case_9.teach: Ovoid periventricular lesions pointing away from the ventricles (Dawson’s fingers) are typical.
Enhancing and non-enhancing lesions together show dissemination in time on a single scan (McDonald criteria).
Spinal MRI and CSF oligoclonal bands support the diagnosis.
items.case_10.hx: 22-year-old with three weeks of worsening morning headaches and vomiting. Papilloedema on examination.
items.case_10.report: CT: dilated lateral and third ventricles with rounded frontal horns and effaced sulci; the fourth ventricle is normal in size. MRI FLAIR: periventricular high signal from transependymal flow.
case_10.teach: Big lateral and third ventricles with a normal fourth point to a block at the cerebral aqueduct.
In hydrocephalus the sulci are squeezed; in atrophy they are wide.
Transependymal CSF flow means the pressure is acutely raised.
items.case_11.hx: 74-year-old retired teacher. Two years of gradually worsening memory; now gets lost driving to familiar places.
items.case_11.report: FDG-PET: bilateral temporoparietal and posterior cingulate hypometabolism with sparing of the sensorimotor and visual cortex. MRI: bilateral hippocampal atrophy. Amyloid PET: positive.
case_11.teach: Alzheimer’s: temporoparietal and posterior cingulate hypometabolism.
Frontotemporal dementia hits frontal and anterior temporal lobes; Lewy body dementia adds occipital loss with a spared posterior cingulate (“island sign”).
Amyloid PET confirms pathology, which matters for anti-amyloid treatments.
items.case_12.hx: 23-year-old with seizures since age 12 that start with a rising feeling in the stomach, then lip-smacking. Febrile seizures as a toddler.
items.case_12.report: MRI: small left hippocampus with high T2/FLAIR signal and loss of internal architecture. FDG-PET: interictal hypometabolism of the left temporal lobe.
case_12.teach: Hippocampal sclerosis: volume loss, high T2 signal and lost internal structure, best seen on thin coronal slices.
Interictal FDG-PET shows the focus as cold; ictal SPECT shows it as hot.
Concordant MRI, EEG and PET make this patient a strong surgical candidate.
items.case_13.hx: 66-year-old with a resting tremor of the right hand and slowness for a year. Parkinson’s disease or essential tremor?
items.case_13.report: DaTscan: reduced uptake in the left putamen, worst posteriorly, giving a “full stop” instead of a “comma”. Mildly reduced on the right.
case_13.teach: Loss starts in the posterior putamen, opposite the side of the symptoms.
The scan is normal in essential tremor and in drug-induced parkinsonism.
It cannot separate Parkinson’s disease from the atypical parkinsonian syndromes.
items.case_14.hx: 29-year-old with a first seizure and occasional headaches.
items.case_14.report: MRI: right parietal cluster of serpiginous flow voids with enhancing vessels and an enlarged draining vein. MRA: nidus with feeding arteries and early venous drainage.
case_14.teach: Flow voids are black because fast blood leaves the slice before it can be imaged.
Arteries connect straight to veins through a nidus, with no capillaries between.
Catheter angiography (DSA) is the gold standard for planning treatment.
items.case_15.hx: Adult on intensive care after cardiac arrest. The clinical tests for brain death are complete; an ancillary perfusion study is requested.
items.case_15.report: HMPAO SPECT: no tracer uptake in the cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum or brainstem (“hollow skull”); scalp activity present, so the injection worked. CTA: no intracranial arterial opacification.
case_15.teach: Brain death is a clinical diagnosis; imaging is an ancillary test where the examination cannot be completed.
Scalp uptake proves the tracer was delivered.
Sedation lowers flow but never abolishes it.
items.case_15.dx.0: Absent cerebral perfusion, consistent with brain death
